signal: Cutover's research showed 309% ROI on work orchestration, on the back of a $35M Series B from Eldridge

email.body1:
Adam, saw Cutover's research put work orchestration at 309% ROI, building on your Series B from Eldridge.

As a RevOps analyst, the bottleneck is rarely signal, it is signal-to-action latency: more in-market accounts surface than the team can act on before they cool, plus the data-hygiene tax. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Cutover off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Adam, quick follow-up for Cutover.

Most RevOps teams lose lift in the gap between a signal firing and a personalized touch going out, and dirty data widens it. Closing that loop is usually where the measurable gains live, not in another tool.

Worth 15 minutes? I will walk you through a teardown of your current outbound, three things I would change. Our best practices alone usually lift reply rates 50 to 70 percent.
email.body3:
Adam, last bit of proof for Cutover.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Cutover's reply rate likely compares to other enterprise-software teams. Want to grab time so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Adam, I will stop reaching out on this one, but did not want to leave you empty-handed.

If tightening signal-to-action latency is not on the roadmap this quarter, no problem at all. RevOps is its own kind of busy, especially mid-scale.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your motion? I will tailor it to Cutover either way.
